_meta.indication: To reduce the risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for heart failure, and urgent heart failure visit in adults with heart failure or with type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and other cardiovascular risk factors

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, double-blind trial (1:1 sotagliflozin vs. placebo)
pivotal_trials.population: Hemodynamically stable adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of heart failure
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to total occurrences (first and subsequent) of CV death, hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), and urgent heart failure visit (UHFV)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary composite incidence rate 51.3 vs 76.4 per 100 patient-years; HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.53, 0.85); p<0.001

nct_ctgov.title: Effect of Sotagliflozin on Cardiovascular Events in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes Post Worsening Heart Failure (SOLOIST-WHF Trial)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter, double-blind trial (1:1 sotagliflozin vs. placebo)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease (eGFR 25 to 60 mL/min/1.73 m2), and either a major CV risk factor or age >=55 years with at least 2 minor CV risk factors
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to total occurrences (first and subsequent) of CV death, hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), and urgent heart failure visit (UHFV)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary composite incidence rate 5.6 vs 7.5 per 100 patient-years; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.63, 0.88); p<0.0004

nct_ctgov.title: Effect of Sotagliflozin on Cardiovascular and Renal Events in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes and Moderate Renal Impairment Who Are at Cardiovascular Risk

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5%) are urinary tract infection, volume depletion, diarrhea, and hypoglycemia. In SOLOIST (INPEFA vs placebo): diarrhea 6.9% vs 4.1%, volume depletion 9.3% vs 8.8%; in SCORED: diarrhea 8.4% vs 6.0%, volume depletion 5.2% vs 4.0%
target_moa: Sotagliflozin is a dual inhibitor of SGLT2 and SGLT1; SGLT2 inhibition reduces renal reabsorption of glucose and sodium, while SGLT1 inhibition reduces intestinal absorption of glucose and sodium

rems.type: DRM and DCN determined that a REMS is not needed to ensure the benefits of sotagliflozin outweigh its risks; risks can be managed via labeling

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was convened because no controversial issues related to pivotal study design, efficacy or safety were identified

basis.text: The application was designated Standard review, not priority

summary.text: NDA 216203 was submitted 5/27/2022 as a standard-review NDA under section 505(b) and approved on a first cycle based on two phase 3 trials (SOLOIST and SCORED); it was the first market approval for sotagliflozin, though a prior Complete Response (22 March 2019) had been issued under separate NDA 210934 for a glycemic control indication. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, or orphan designation applied, and no REMS or advisory committee meeting was required.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA), originally submitted and received on December 20, 2021, and resubmitted on May 27, 2022, and your amendments, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Inpefa (sotagliflozin) tablets.

NDA 216203 is the first market approval filing for sotagliflozin, indicated for the treatment of HF morbidity and mortality. However, sotagliflozin has previously undergone regulatory review for a glycemic control indication. On 22 March 2018, the Applicant submitted NDA 210934 seeking an indication to improve glycemic control when used with insulin in adult patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus
No Advisory Committee meeting was convened because no controversial issues related to pivotal study design, efficacy or safety results and overall determination of benefit-risk were identified.
